teaches: أرض carries no feminine marker at all and is feminine only because the closed registry declares it so
a second registry member proves the decision is exact closed-list membership, never a shape rule
no declared lexeme at all never survives as a default feminine
قمر is masculine and outside the registry; shape gives it no vote here
a regular taa-marbuta feminine is a DIFFERENT (morphological) mechanism outside this closed lexical registry's scope -- it abstains here too, never inferred from its own shape
a near-collision surface built on a registered root (أرضية, "flooring") is NOT the registered lexeme itself; exact membership, never a substring or root match, decides this
